bibl.title: Linked Data Annotation Without the Pointy Brackets: Introducing Recogito 2

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: With Recogito 2, we aim to provide an environment for efficient semantic annotation—i.e. the task of enriching content with references to controlled vocabularies—in order to facilitate links between online data.

span.label: semantic geo-annotation of texts and maps with gazetteer URIs
span.quote: While Recogito 2 provides an online workspace for general-purpose document annotation, it is particularly well-suited for geo-annotation, i.e. annotating documents with references to gazetteers, and supports the annotation of both texts and images (e.g. digitized maps).

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: Beginning in February 2016, and supported by renewed funding from the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation, we therefore started to develop a new version of Recogito, redesigned from the bottom up, with the aim of establishing the technical infrastructure for an open, collaborative, generally usable, and useful, work environment.

span.label: Geo-resolution stayed the productivity bottleneck of the workflow even after a UI redesign.
span.quote: But it is obvious that geo-resolution remained the productivity bottleneck in our workflow.

span.label: Gazetteers are so far the only controlled vocabulary the tool supports for semantic annotation.
span.quote: At the time of writing, gazetteers are the only type of controlled vocabulary available for semantic annotation.

span.label: The tool was still unreleased at the time of writing, with public release only scheduled.
span.quote: Already available for testing at http://recogito.pelagios.org , its formal release to the public is scheduled for December 2016.

span.label: An annotation is presented as somebody's claim, not as established fact.
span.quote: On the one hand, annotation works as a suitable conceptual metaphor, since it carries the connotation that the association being made ought not to be considered certain fact; rather somebody (a human editor or an automated geo-parsing script) is making a claim

span.label: Whether the vocabulary is ontological is a social fact about a community, not a property of the data.
span.quote: rightfully point out that whether a term is ontological or not is a purely social matter, not a technical, nor formal one

span.label: The approach's success is credited to a shared vocabulary that already existed for that period and region.
span.quote: This was not least due to the fact that for this period of time and geographic area, a suitable, focused historical URI-based gazetteer existed already, and was widely acknowledged among the scholarly community

span.label: an annotation - AN ASSERTION OF AN INTERPRETATION, NOT A STATEMENT OF FACT: the paper says the association ought not to be considered certain fact and that somebody - explicitly either a human editor or an automated geo-parsing script - is making a claim; the annotator's kind is part of what the annotation records
span.quote: On the one hand, annotation works as a suitable conceptual metaphor, since it carries the connotation that the association being made ought not to be considered certain fact; rather somebody (a human editor or an automated geo-parsing script) is making a claim

span.label: ontological annotation - DEFINED BY COMMUNITY AGREEMENT, NOT BY FORMALISM: formal annotations use formally defined terms, and ontological ones are those whose terminology has a commonly understood meaning according to a shared conceptualization - so the top of the hierarchy is a social condition, and the authors endorse the point that it is a purely social matter and not a technical or formal one
span.quote: Ontological annotations, finally, are formal annotations where terminology has a commonly understood meaning according to a shared conceptualization. Oren et al. rightfully point out that whether a term is ontological or not is a purely social matter, not a technical, nor formal one

span.label: the benefit of Linked Data - A SHARED SOCIAL UNDERSTANDING, NOT MACHINE-READABILITY: the paper puts the value of semantic annotation in the shared vocabulary rather than in the data being machine-processable, which is the answer this project owes to the objection that formalising meaning loses what matters
span.quote: The benefit of the ontological—or semantic—annotation, and in fact of Linked Data as a whole, is therefore not so much the machine-readability of the data as such, but rather that it is represents a shared social understanding, expressed with a shared vocabulary

span.label: extends → Recogito 1 (Simon et al. 2015)
span.quote: Unlike Recogito 1, Recogito 2 now supports a combination of free-text commentary and semantic annotations (URI-based references to terms in controlled vocabularies).

span.label: contradicts → Pundit (Grassi et al. 2012, 2013)
span.quote: However, Pundit confronts the user with the full breadth of technical terminology.

span.label: annotation —is-a→ claim
span.quote: On the one hand, annotation works as a suitable conceptual metaphor, since it carries the connotation that the association being made ought not to be considered certain fact; rather somebody (a human editor or an automated geo-parsing script) is making a claim

span.label: place —operationalised-as→ gazetteer URI
span.quote: Pelagios advocates the idea that whenever you refer to a place in your data, you should do so using a gazetteer URI

span.label: Shared gazetteer URIs are what joins otherwise isolated datasets; the gazetteer becomes the backbone of the graph.
span.quote: By expressing the places through the use of shared gazetteer URIs, otherwise isolated datasets become implicitly joined up to an interconnected graph, with the gazetteers as their central backbone

span.label: The tool deliberately targets a gap in existing tools: manual intervention and editorial control, in the service of data quality.
span.quote: by emphasizing the development of mechanisms for manual intervention and editorial control that support the curation of quality data

span.label: Annotation had been restricted to the technically expert, and to tools that offered little interoperability.
span.quote: has tended to be restricted to researchers with technical expertise, and to tools that offer little to no opportunity for interoperability and data exchange

span.label: semantic annotation
span.quote: the task of enriching content with references to controlled vocabularies

span.label: geo-annotation
span.quote: annotating documents with references to gazetteers
